questions.prompt: Where did the most rain ever recorded fall in 24 hours (WMO)?
questions.teaser: Where did the most rain ever fall in one day?
questions.turnsOut: Foc-Foc, 2,290 m up on the volcanic island of La Réunion: 1,825 mm in 24 hours on 7–8 January 1966, as Tropical Cyclone Denise passed. The same storm set the 12-hour record too: 1,144 mm.
questions.sourceTitle: WMO Weather and Climate Extremes Archive: records table (31 July 2025)

questions.prompt: Where is the lowest land on Earth that is not under water or ice?
questions.teaser: Where is the lowest dry land on Earth?

targets.label: The shores of the Dead Sea

questions.turnsOut: The shores of the Dead Sea: on 31 August 2026 the lake stood 441.33 m below sea level. It drops about a metre a year as the Jordan and the Yarmouk are dammed upstream and its water is pumped away; in 1900 it stood at 392 m below.
questions.sourceTitle: Dead Sea level since 1976 (Israel Water Authority, data.gov.il)
questions.licence: Open government data; fact, own wording

questions.prompt: Where is the highest average annual temperature on record, measured from 1960 to 1966 (Meteorological Magazine)?
questions.teaser: Where is the hottest place on average, all year round?
questions.authority: D. E. Pedgley, Meteorological Magazine (UK Met Office), 1967
questions.turnsOut: Dallol, in Ethiopia's Danakil Depression: a prospecting camp's weather station there averaged 41 °C (106 °F) by day and 28 °C (83 °F) by night over 1960–66, hotter on both counts than anywhere in the world tables of the time.
questions.sourceTitle: Air temperature at Dallol, Ethiopia (Meteorological Magazine, September 1967)
